app.title: River-district daily water supply-demand scheduling model
app.summary: A person either runs the bundled sample inputs or uploads a ZIP of daily input tables and static parameter tables, then starts the run. The model works through each district day by day. It adds up inflow and demand, turns water levels into storage with each district's level-storage curve, and works out the shortage that has to come from outside and the drainage above the drain level. Totals across all districts are shown as headline numbers. The person then picks one district to read its daily results table and a chart of inflow, demand and shortage, and downloads that district's results as an Excel file.

task.text: Simulate the daily water supply-demand balance of many districts, find how much shortage each one has, and export each district's results.

data.text: Daily tables with one column per district, covering demand components and inflow sources. Static tables give each district's level-storage curve, its starting, target and drainage water levels, which reservoirs it contains, and the diversion rules of the sluices. The output is one daily balance table per district.
data.item: a district's daily water balance series

stage.text: running a water balance scheduling simulation on prepared inputs, before planning or reporting

mechanism.text: A sidebar loads the sample data or an uploaded ZIP and runs the simulation. The main area shows headline totals for all districts. A district selector chooses which daily table and line chart are shown, and which district is offered for Excel download.

field.text: daily supply-demand balance scheduling in water resources engineering

workflow.name: run a daily balance simulation across zones and inspect each zone's result

steps.here: One button runs the bundled sample. Otherwise a ZIP of input_*.txt and static_*.txt files is uploaded, and its run button stays disabled until a file is chosen. A folder nested inside the ZIP is detected.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: For each district and each day, the model adds up the inflow sources and the demand components. It converts water levels to storage through an interpolated level-storage curve and carries storage forward from one day to the next. It also computes the external shortage, the drainage above the drain level, and the room left to store more water.

steps.step: track progress toward a target or a total
steps.here: Four metrics show how many districts were processed and the total demand, total inflow and total shortage across all districts.
A selectbox lists the districts that have output files. The chosen district's full daily results appear as a table.

steps.step: compare quantities over time for the selected item
steps.here: A line chart plots total inflow, total demand and shortage against date for the selected district.
A download button saves the selected district's daily table as an Excel workbook.

distinctive: Each district has a level-storage curve that is interpolated linearly in both directions, so water levels and storage volumes can be converted either way.
Shortage is the demand that inflow cannot meet, and it is supplied from outside the district. Storage above a set drainage level is drained away each day.
Reservoir inflow is added up for each district from a table that lists which reservoirs each district contains.
Some districts run in a dynamic-balance mode: their external supply is set so that inflow exactly meets demand.
Per-district outputs are also added together into an all-district summary series.
